title: Budgeted web research job contract with run-context cost attribution
summary: Package the existing search, scrape and browser-agent steps as one research run in the Model Plane: input {prompt, urls?, output schema?, max cost/credits, effort}, output {status, data, partial, partialSchemaValid, stopReason such as credit_limit_reached, creditsUsed}, with one active run per thread (409 thread_busy plus the running run id). Quarry accepts a signed run-context header {requestId, parentRunId} from the Model Plane so its cost events attach to the parent run and are not billed twice.
whyItMatters: A predictable, budgeted research call gives other features, and any future external API user, one contract with partial results and a clear stop reason instead of stitching step-level agent routes together. Accurate per-run cost in the Model Plane cost service depends on Quarry knowing the parent run.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Firecrawl (api-surface fc-020 agent job and fc-022 threads; fc-021 trusted internal calls with requestId and shouldBill)
others: Apify (Actor runs with max-charge limits, DOC)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: research-agent job API: 1 of 4 sources (Firecrawl), unique; internal service call attribution: 1 of 4 (Firecrawl)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: POST /agent {prompt, urls?, schema?, maxCredits, effort, strictConstrainToURLs, webhook} returns an id; GET returns {status, data, partial, partialSchemaValid, stopReason, creditsUsed, pendingApproval}; a thread rejects a new turn with 409 while a run is active. Internal agent services call the public endpoints with a shared-secret block {requestId, shouldBill} so tool calls are attributed to the parent run; Verevon should use its stronger scoped service tokens plus a signed header rather than one shared secret.

verevonToday.gap: Model Plane owns sessions/runs and Quarry exposes step-level /v1/agent/runs, but there is no single research-job contract with output schema, budget, stopReason and partial results; propagation of a parent run id into Quarry cost events was not verified; the gateway browser path depends on the grant fix in R-t2-01-05.

approach: Model Plane: add a research-run type over the existing sessions/runs with schema validation (using the json format from R-t2-01-04), a budget and partial-result semantics; it calls Quarry search/scrape/agent steps under service tokens. Ingestion Plane: accept a signed run-context header and tag cost events with run id; widen service scopes deliberately (map yes; crawl starts stay approval-gated so 'Model proposes, Quarry executes' holds). Cost service integration records per-run cost.
planeOwner: Model Plane (run contract) with Ingestion Plane (run-context attribution)
risks: Cost runaway (enforce the budget server-side); schema-valid but wrong outputs; ZDR must hold across every step.

verevon.exactGap: A research pipeline already exists but as a chat feature: model-gateway deep_research.rs (plan, concurrent search, read, synthesize, cited document artifact) runs under a session run when a request sets deepResearch, with spend caps (sub-queries, pages read, corpus chars, wall clock), a coverage report with a halt_code stop reason and a cancelled/partial outcome, yet it is in-process, dies with the stream, is not an addressable job, takes no caller budget or output schema, and has no thread-busy guard (no thread_busy or 409 concept found in Model Plane). Quarry exposes only step-level routes (/v1/search, /v1/extract, /v1/agent/runs, job listing) and meters billing UsageEvents keyed by its own request id with free-form metadata, while execution-core's web tools send only a bearer and x-quarry-org, so no parent run id reaches Quarry and Quarry usage flows to billing-core rather than the Model Plane cost-core (cost-core ingestion of Quarry cost was not traced). A USD ceiling exists only for browser runs (Quarry AgentConstraints.max_cost_usd, gateway max_cost_usd); there is no credits budget for search or scrape.

verevon.constraints: Model Plane owns the run and its cost; Quarry only executes and meters and must treat a run-context header as advisory attribution, never authority (signed, org-checked). ZDR must hold across every step: deep research is already refused for waived runs and the chat pipeline persists nothing precisely because it dies with the stream, so a durable job record must not retain content for ZDR callers. Budgets must be enforced server-side in the Model Plane, since Quarry usage reaches billing-core asynchronously. Crawl starts remain approval-gated (Model proposes, Quarry executes).
verevon.approachAdjustment: Do not build a new research-run type from raw steps: promote the existing deep_research pipeline to an addressable run (GET status, partial results, stopReason mapped from halt_code, one active run per thread returning 409 and the running run id), map the caller budget onto the existing caps plus a credit or USD ceiling, and add output-schema validation only after the JSON-format item lands. Add the signed run-context header as a separate small cross-plane change (web_tools.rs and the model-gateway Quarry client send requestId and parentRunId; Quarry writes them into UsageEvent.metadata). Defer the external-API-user justification until such a consumer exists.
verevon.effortNote: Reworded scope (addressable wrapper over the existing pipeline, budget mapping, thread-busy guard, run-context attribution) is M because the pipeline and its session run already exist. Output-schema validation and fully durable partial state would return it to L.
verevon.verdictReason: The item proposes packaging steps that deep_research already packages for chat. The real gaps are addressability, a caller budget, thread-busy semantics and run-context attribution to Quarry; reword to those.
